paper_metadata.title: Outcomes of newly diagnosed idiopathic generalized epilepsy syndromes in a non-pediatric setting

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the recruitment source, period, and setting. Inclusion/exclusion criteria are based on established ILAE guidelines, and baseline characteristics are well-defined for the analyzed cohort.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Adolescent and adult patients with suspected seizure disorders were referred to a specialist first seizure service by general practitioners, accident and emergency physicians and other clinicians.
items.reasoning: The source population is clearly defined as adolescent and adult patients referred to a specific regional specialist service.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: A total of 890 patients were diagnosed with epilepsy after presenting to the First Seizure Clinic at the Epilepsy Unit in the Western Infirmary in Glasgow, between August 1981 and May 2001.
items.reasoning: The recruitment process via a First Seizure Clinic over a 20-year period is explicitly stated.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: between August 1981 and May 2001.
items.reasoning: The specific dates for the recruitment window are provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Epilepsy Unit in the Western Infirmary in Glasgow
items.reasoning: The specific clinical setting and geographic location are identified.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Seizure types and epilepsy syndromes were classified according to ILAE guidelines at the time of analysis (1, 7). ... Patients who did not return for review or were persistently non-adherent to their prescribed medication were excluded from analysis.
items.reasoning: The study uses standardized ILAE criteria for inclusion and specifies reasons for exclusion.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: Of 890 patients, 118 (13%) met the criteria for IGES.
items.reasoning: While the number of eligible patients is clear, the text does not specify how many eligible individuals declined to participate initially, though it notes 15 were lost to follow-up.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: The median age at epilepsy onset was 17 years (range 5–51) and that at diagnosis was 18 years (range 9–71). ... 103 (47 males, 56 females)
items.reasoning: Age, gender, and syndrome distribution are provided for the study sample.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study reports a loss to follow-up of approximately 12.7% (15/118) for the IGES subgroup. While the reasons for exclusion (non-adherence/no return) are mentioned, there is no detailed comparison of characteristics between those lost and those who completed the study.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: Of the entire cohort of 890 adult and adolescent patients, 118 (13%) fitted the criteria for a diagnosis of IGES. Fifteen patients were lost to followup and the remaining 103... were included in the outcome analysis.
items.reasoning: 87% of the identified IGES cohort was analyzed, which is generally considered acceptable.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (remission) is clearly defined using a standard 12-month seizure-free threshold. The measurement was consistent for all participants and based on clinical follow-up.

items.evidence_snippet: The primary end point was seizure freedom for a minimum of 12 months on an unchanged treatment schedule.
items.reasoning: The definition of remission is precise and follows standard epilepsy research criteria.
